requirements.requirement: Place curl on an apt hold so it stays at its current installed version (7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19) on node1
requirements.summary: apt-mark hold curl was applied and confirmed via apt-mark showhold and dpkg --get-selections (status 'hold'/'hi').

requirements.requirement: Confirm the hold is effective against a system update (curl excluded from upgrade)
requirements.summary: apt-get upgrade -s and dist-upgrade -s simulations both show curl untouched; dpkg version unchanged after simulation.

requirements.requirement: Hold persists and curl remains functional and excluded from updates after a reboot
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id b185f188... captured with hold healthy; node rebooted (acknowledged, briefly unreachable, then reachable with new boot_id 089b6567...); post-restart dpkg shows curl status 'hi' at same version, curl --version works, and upgrade simulation still excludes curl. Boot-identity values match the fixed before_prepare/after_executor lifecycle snapshots, corroborating the transition.

overall_summary: The executor applied an apt-mark hold on curl at its pre-existing version, verified via both upgrade and dist-upgrade simulations that curl is excluded from updates, and additionally ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol showing a genuine reboot (boot_id changed) after which the hold, curl functionality, and update-exclusion all persisted. All material outcomes of the task instruction are directly and coherently satisfied by captured evidence, and the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots corroborate the restart transition.
limitations: No actual full 'apt-get upgrade' was executed (only -s dry-run simulations), so real-world upgrade behavior beyond the simulation is inferred rather than directly observed, though this is a reasonable and non-destructive verification approach.
The restart/reboot was not required by the public task contract but was performed per the separate provider-wide protocol; evidence for it is complete and consistent.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (apt-mark hold, the reboot) are directly tied to satisfying the task and to the mandatory restart evidence protocol. No packages were actually upgraded (only simulated with -s), which is an appropriately non-destructive verification choice. Post-reboot temporary-file diffs are just systemd-private per-boot service directories churned by the restart itself, not executor-created residue. No failed services, package-health issues, or unnecessary mutations were observed in the timeline.
